modelEssay.title: The Importance of Having a Sense of Social Responsibility
modelEssay.content:
In today's rapidly changing world, the significance of possessing a sense of social responsibility cannot be overstated. It is a fundamental quality that shapes individuals into active and constructive members of society.

Firstly, a sense of social responsibility fosters a spirit of contribution and service. Individuals who are socially responsible are more likely to engage in volunteer work, donate to charities, and participate in community projects, thereby enhancing the well-being of others. Moreover, this sense of responsibility also encourages people to be environmentally conscious, conserving resources and reducing pollution.

In conclusion, having a sense of social responsibility is crucial for the betterment of society. It not only promotes personal growth but also strengthens the social fabric by encouraging cooperation and mutual support among citizens.

transcript.text: Today our guest is Rosie Mullander, who works as a Features Editor for a fashion magazine.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 今天我们的嘉宾是Rosie Mullander，她在一家时尚杂志担任专题编辑。

transcript.text: Hi, Rosie.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你好，Rosie。

transcript.text: You're a Features Editor at one of the most widely read women's magazines in the UK.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你是英国最广泛阅读的女性杂志之一的专题编辑。

transcript.text: What kind of responsibilities does that job entail?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这份工作涉及哪些职责？

transcript.text: We spend our days looking at ideas from journalists, writing copy for the magazine and website and editing.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们整天都在审视记者的创意，为杂志和网站撰写稿件并进行编辑。

transcript.text: We do random things like asking people in the street questions and testing sports clothing.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们做各种随机的事情，比如在街上向人们提问和测试运动服装。

transcript.text: We also do less tangible things like understanding what our readers want.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们还做一些不那么有形的事情，比如理解读者想要什么。

transcript.text: It's certainly varied and sometimes bizarre.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 这当然多样化，有时甚至很奇特。

transcript.text: During your working day, what kind of work might you typically do?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 在你的工作日里，你通常会做哪些工作？

transcript.text: My day mainly incorporates responding to emails, writing and editing stories and coming up with new feature ideas.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我的一天主要包括回复电子邮件、撰写和编辑故事以及提出新的专题创意。

transcript.text: How does the job of Features Editor differ from that of Fashion Editor or other editorial positions?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 专题编辑的工作与时尚编辑或其他编辑职位有何不同？

transcript.text: The Features Team deals with articles such as careers, reports, confidence and confessions, everything except fashion and beauty.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 专题团队处理的文章包括职业、报告、自信和自白等，除了时尚和美容之外的所有内容。

transcript.text: A lot of people believe that working at a magazine is a glamorous job.
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 许多人认为在杂志工作是一份光鲜亮丽的工作。

transcript.text: Is this an accurate representation of what you do?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 这准确地描述了你所做的工作吗？

transcript.text: I'd say it's glamorous to an extent, but not in the way it's portrayed in films.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我会说它在一定程度上是光鲜的，但不像电影中描绘的那样。

transcript.text: We do have our moments, such as interviewing celebrities and attending parties, which is a huge thrill.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我们确实有这样的时刻，比如采访名人和参加派对，这非常令人兴奋。

transcript.text: Ultimately, though, we're the same as our readers, but working in a job we're all very lucky to have.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 但最终，我们和读者一样，只是从事着我们都很幸运拥有的一份工作。

transcript.text: Did you have to overcome any difficulties to reach this point in your career?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你在职业生涯中达到这一点时，是否需要克服任何困难？

transcript.text: How did you manage to do this?
transcript.speaker: M
transcript.translation: 你是如何做到这一点的？

transcript.text: I had to be really persistent, and it was very hard work.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我必须非常坚持，而且工作非常辛苦。

transcript.text: After three years of working in a petrol station and doing unpaid work, I still hadn't managed to get an entry-level job.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 在加油站工作三年并做无偿工作后，我仍然没有找到一份入门级工作。

transcript.text: I was lucky that my last desperate attempt led to a job.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我很幸运，我最后的绝望尝试带来了一份工作。

transcript.text: I told myself that all experiences make you a better journalist in the long run, and luckily I was right.
transcript.speaker: F
transcript.translation: 我告诉自己，从长远来看，所有经历都会让你成为一名更好的记者，幸运的是我是对的。

transcript.text: Passage 1.
transcript.translation: 段落1。

transcript.text: Related to the use-it-or-lose-it law is the keep-moving principle.
transcript.translation: 与用进废退法则相关的是保持移动原则。

transcript.text: We learn about stagnation from nature.
transcript.translation: 我们从自然界学习到停滞不前的问题。

transcript.text: A river that stops moving gets smelly.
transcript.translation: 一条停止流动的河流会变得发臭。

transcript.text: The same thing happens to people who stop moving, either mentally or physically.
transcript.translation: 同样的事情也会发生在停止移动的人身上，无论是精神上还是身体上。

transcript.text: Those who play contact sports know that the player who usually gets hurt the most is the one who is standing still.
transcript.translation: 参与接触性运动的人都知道，通常受伤最严重的球员是那个站着不动的人。

transcript.text: Of course, you'll need some time to catch your breath every so often, but the essential message is keep moving, extending and learning.
transcript.translation: 当然，你时不时需要一些时间来喘口气，但核心信息是保持移动、延伸和学习。

transcript.text: Ships last a lot longer when they go to sea than when they stay in the harbor.
transcript.translation: 船在海上航行时比停在港口时寿命更长。

transcript.text: The same is true for airplanes.
transcript.translation: 飞机也是如此。

transcript.text: You don't preserve an airplane by keeping it on the ground.
transcript.translation: 你不是通过让飞机停在地面上来保存它。

transcript.text: You preserve it by keeping it in service.
transcript.translation: 你是通过让它保持使用状态来保存它。

transcript.text: We also get to live a long, healthy life by staying in service.
transcript.translation: 我们也是通过保持活跃状态来过上长寿、健康的生活。

transcript.text: Longevity statistics reveal that the average person doesn't last very long after retirement.
transcript.translation: 寿命统计数据显示，普通人在退休后不会活得很长。

transcript.text: The moral here is don't retire.
transcript.translation: 这里的寓意是不要退休。

transcript.text: If a fellow says, I'm 94 years old and I've worked all my life, we need to realize that is how we got to be 94, by staying involved.
transcript.translation: 如果一个人说，我94岁了，我一生都在工作，我们需要认识到，正是通过保持参与，我们才活到了94岁。

transcript.text: George Bernard Shaw won a Nobel Prize when he was nearly 70.
transcript.translation: 乔治·萧伯纳在近70岁时获得了诺贝尔奖。

transcript.text: Benjamin Franklin produced some of his best writings at the age of 84.
transcript.translation: 本杰明·富兰克林在84岁时创作了一些他最好的作品。

transcript.text: And Pablo Picasso put brush to canvas right through his 80s.
transcript.translation: 而巴勃罗·毕加索一直到80多岁还在画布上挥笔作画。

transcript.text: Isn't the issue how old we think we are?
transcript.translation: 问题难道不是我们认为自己多大年纪吗？

transcript.text: A bonus with the keep moving principle is that while we keep moving, we don't have a chance to worry.
transcript.translation: 保持移动原则的一个额外好处是，当我们保持移动时，我们没有机会去担心。

transcript.text: Hence, we avoid the dreaded paralysis by analysis.
transcript.translation: 因此，我们避免了可怕的因分析而瘫痪。

transcript.text: Passage 2.
transcript.translation: 篇章2。

transcript.text: In 2014, one in 16 Americans visited the hospital emergency room for home injuries.
transcript.translation: 2014年，每16名美国人中就有一人因家庭伤害而去了医院急诊室。

transcript.text: One of the main causes of these accidents, a wandering mind.
transcript.translation: 这些事故的主要原因之一是注意力不集中。

transcript.text: By one estimate, people daydream through nearly half of their waking hours.
transcript.translation: 据估计，人们在清醒时间里近一半都在做白日梦。

transcript.text: Psychologists have recently focused on the tendency to think about something other than the task one is doing.
transcript.translation: 心理学家最近关注了人们在执行任务时倾向于思考其他事情的倾向。

transcript.text: For one experiment, researchers developed an app to analyse the relationship between daydreaming and happiness.
transcript.translation: 在一项实验中，研究人员开发了一款应用程序来分析白日梦与幸福之间的关系。

transcript.text: They found that the average person's mind wandered most frequently, about 65% of the time, during personal activities, such as brushing their teeth and combing their hair.
transcript.translation: 他们发现，普通人在个人活动，如刷牙和梳头时，注意力不集中的频率最高，约占65%的时间。

transcript.text: Respondents' minds tended to wander more when they felt upset rather than happy.
transcript.translation: 受访者在感到沮丧而非快乐时，注意力更易分散。

transcript.text: They were more likely to wander toward pleasant topics than unpleasant ones.
transcript.translation: 他们更可能转向愉快的话题，而不是不愉快的话题。

transcript.text: How do daydreams affect daydreamers?
transcript.translation: 白日梦如何影响做白日梦的人？

transcript.text: A wandering mind leaves us vulnerable when driving.
transcript.translation: 开车时注意力不集中会使我们处于危险之中。

transcript.text: In one study, researchers interviewed 955 people involved in traffic accidents.
transcript.translation: 在一项研究中，研究人员采访了955名涉及交通事故的人。

transcript.text: The majority of them reported having daydreamed just before the accident.
transcript.translation: 他们中的大多数报告称在事故发生前刚刚做了白日梦。

transcript.text: Yet other research suggests that daydreaming has benefits.
transcript.translation: 然而，其他研究表明白日梦也有好处。

transcript.text: Researchers have found that it gives us a chance to think about our goals, and it also seems to increase creativity.
transcript.translation: 研究人员发现，它让我们有机会思考目标，并且似乎还能增加创造力。

transcript.text: In one experiment, 145 undergraduates completed four unusual uses tasks, each requiring them to list as many uses as possible for an everyday object.
transcript.translation: 在一项实验中，145名本科生完成了四项不寻常用途任务，每项任务要求他们尽可能多地列出日常物品的用途。

transcript.text: After the first pair of tasks was completed, one group of participants was assigned an undemanding activity intended to cause their minds to wander.
transcript.translation: 在完成第一对任务后，一组参与者被分配了一项不费力的活动，旨在引发他们的思绪漫游。

transcript.text: When all the participants proceeded to the second pair of tasks, the daydreamers performed 40% better than the others.
transcript.translation: 当所有参与者继续进行第二对任务时，做白日梦的组比其他人表现好40%。

transcript.text: Dating from as far back as the 12th century, they are claimed to be the rarest historic buildings in Western Europe.
transcript.translation: 追溯到12世纪，它们据称是西欧最稀有的历史建筑。

transcript.text: These buildings offer vital insights into Scandinavia's Viking past.
transcript.translation: 这些建筑提供了对斯堪的纳维亚维京过去的深刻见解。

transcript.text: But now, with only 30 wooden churches remaining and their condition deteriorating, experts are working to preserve the structures for future generations.
transcript.translation: 但现在，随着仅存30座木制教堂且状况恶化，专家们正努力为子孙后代保存这些结构。

transcript.text: Some of these spectacular churches are no more than small buildings, barely 4 metres wide and 6 metres tall.
transcript.translation: 其中一些壮观的教堂只不过是小建筑，宽度仅4米，高度仅6米。

transcript.text: Others are much larger structures that soar up to 40 metres into the cold air.
transcript.translation: 其他则是大得多的建筑，高耸入寒冷的空气中，高达40米。

transcript.text: Most consist of timber frames that rest on stone blocks.
transcript.translation: 大多数由木框架构成，木框架放置在石块上。

transcript.text: This means that they have no foundations.
transcript.translation: 这意味着它们没有地基。

transcript.text: Although many of the churches appear from the outside to be complex structures, they normally feature only a single storey, but numerous different roof levels.
transcript.translation: 尽管许多教堂从外观上看是复杂的结构，但它们通常只有一层，但有许多不同的屋顶层次。

transcript.text: Staff from the Norwegian government have carried out conservation work on 10 of the churches over the past two years.
transcript.translation: 挪威政府工作人员在过去两年中对其中10座教堂进行了保护工作。

transcript.text: Most of these churches date from between the 12th and 14th centuries.
transcript.translation: 这些教堂大多建于12世纪至14世纪之间。

transcript.text: Other churches were conserved in previous years.
transcript.translation: 其他教堂在往年得到了保护。

transcript.text: So far, specialists have worked to add preservative materials to the churches' exteriors.
transcript.translation: 到目前为止，专家们致力于在教堂外部添加防腐材料。

transcript.text: They also replaced rotting roofs and halted the sinking of the churches into the ground.
transcript.translation: 他们还替换了腐烂的屋顶，并阻止了教堂沉入地面。

transcript.text: In two cases, huge machines had been used to lift the buildings up to 30 centimetres into the air.
transcript.translation: 在两起案例中，使用了巨型机器将建筑提升到空中高达30厘米。

transcript.text: This was accomplished so that the team could examine and repair the churches' original medieval stone blocks.
transcript.translation: 这样做是为了团队能够检查和修复教堂原有的中世纪石块。

transcript.text: The team plans to return to around a dozen of the buildings to assess progress and consider further action.
transcript.translation: 团队计划返回约十二座建筑，以评估进展并考虑进一步行动。

transcript.text: The earliest three-standing wooden church was probably built in Norway in around 1080.
transcript.translation: 最早的三座现存木制教堂可能建于1080年左右的挪威。

transcript.text: However, the largest known wooden churches were built from the 1130s onwards.
transcript.translation: 然而，已知最大的木制教堂建于1130年代以后。

transcript.text: This period was one of inter-elite rivalry, in which nobles sought to increase their influence by funding the construction of churches and other buildings.
transcript.translation: 这个时期是精英间竞争的时期，贵族们通过资助教堂和其他建筑的建设来寻求增加影响力。

transcript.text: The reason for constructing the buildings from wood is probably that ideally proportioned, straight and slender timber was available in large quantities in Scandinavia's vast pine forests.
transcript.translation: 用木材建造这些建筑的原因可能是斯堪的纳维亚广阔的松林中大量提供了比例理想、笔直纤细的木材。

transcript.text: As wood was so plentiful, it was cheaper to use than the stone used in the buildings of other European cultures.
transcript.translation: 由于木材如此丰富，它比其他欧洲文化建筑中使用的石头更便宜。

transcript.text: The area's shipbuilding tradition, partly established by the Vikings, also meant that sophisticated carpentry was a major aspect of the local culture.
transcript.translation: 该地区的造船传统，部分由维京人建立，也意味着精细木工是当地文化的主要方面。

transcript.text: The complex style of the medieval wooden church carvings and the skills used to make them almost certainly derive from the ancient Viking tradition.
transcript.translation: 中世纪木制教堂雕刻的复杂风格和制作技能几乎肯定源于古老的维京传统。

transcript.text: In last week's lecture, we discussed the characteristics of the newly born offspring of several mammals.
transcript.translation: 在上周的讲座中，我们讨论了几种哺乳动物新生后代的特征。

transcript.text: You probably remember that human infants are less developed physically than other mammals of the same age.
transcript.translation: 你可能记得，人类婴儿在身体发育上不如同龄的其他哺乳动物。

transcript.text: But in today's lecture, we'll look at three very interesting studies that hint at the surprising abilities of human babies.
transcript.translation: 但在今天的讲座中，我们将看三项非常有趣的研究，这些研究暗示了人类婴儿的惊人能力。

transcript.text: In the first study, three-year-olds watched two videos shown side by side, each featuring a different researcher, one of whom they'd met once, two years earlier.
transcript.translation: 在第一项研究中，三岁儿童观看了并排显示的两个视频，每个视频展示不同的研究人员，其中一位他们在两年前见过一次。

transcript.text: The children spent longer watching the video showing the researcher they hadn't met.
transcript.translation: 孩子们花了更长时间观看展示他们未见过的研究人员的视频。

transcript.text: This is consistent with young children's usual tendency to look longer at things that aren't familiar.
transcript.translation: 这与幼儿通常倾向于更长时间观看不熟悉的事物的倾向一致。

transcript.text: And really, this is amazing.
transcript.translation: 而且，这真的令人惊叹。

transcript.text: It suggests the children remembered the researcher they'd met just one time when they were only one-year-olds.
transcript.translation: 这表明，孩子们记住了他们在仅一岁时只见过一次的研究人员。

transcript.text: Of course, as most of us forget memories from our first few years as we grow older, these early, long-term memories will likely be lost in subsequent years.
transcript.translation: 当然，随着年龄增长，我们大多数人会忘记最初几年的记忆，这些早期的长期记忆可能会在随后的几年中丧失。

transcript.text: Our second study is about music.
transcript.translation: 我们的第二项研究是关于音乐的。

transcript.text: For this study, researchers played music to babies through speakers located on either side of a human face.
transcript.translation: 在这项研究中，研究人员通过位于人脸两侧的扬声器向婴儿播放音乐。

transcript.text: They waited until the babies got bored and averted their gaze from the face.
transcript.translation: 他们等待直到婴儿感到厌烦并将视线从脸上移开。

transcript.text: And then they changed the mood of the music, either from sad to happy or the other way around.
transcript.translation: 然后他们改变了音乐的情绪，要么从悲伤变为快乐，要么反之。

transcript.text: This mood switch made no difference to the three-month-olds, but for the nine-month-olds, it was enough to renew their interest, and they started looking again in the direction of the face.
transcript.translation: 这种情绪转换对三个月大的婴儿没有影响，但对九个月大的婴儿来说，足以重新激发他们的兴趣，他们开始再次看向脸的方向。

transcript.text: This suggests that babies of that age can tell the difference between a happy melody and a sad tune.
transcript.translation: 这表明，这个年龄的婴儿能够区分快乐的旋律和悲伤的曲调。

transcript.text: Our final study is from 1980, but it's still relevant today.
transcript.translation: 我们的最后一项研究来自1980年，但至今仍然相关。

transcript.text: In fact, it's one of the most famous pieces of research about infant emotion ever published.
transcript.translation: 事实上，它是有史以来发表的最著名的婴儿情感研究之一。

transcript.text: The study involved ordinary adults watching video clips of babies nine months or younger.
transcript.translation: 这项研究涉及普通成年人观看九个月或更小婴儿的视频片段。

transcript.text: In the video clips, the babies made various facial expressions in response to real-life events, including playful interactions and painful ones.
transcript.translation: 在视频片段中，婴儿对现实生活中的事件做出了各种面部表情，包括互动和痛苦事件。

transcript.text: The adult observers were able to reliably discern an assortment of emotions on the babies' faces.
transcript.translation: 成年观察者能够可靠地辨别婴儿脸上的各种情绪。

transcript.text: These emotions included interest, joy, surprise, sadness, anger, disgust, contempt, and fear.
transcript.translation: 这些情绪包括兴趣、喜悦、惊讶、悲伤、愤怒、厌恶、轻蔑和恐惧。

transcript.text: Next week, we'll be looking at this last study more closely.
transcript.translation: 下周，我们将更仔细地研究这项最后的研究。

transcript.text: In fact, we will be viewing some of the video clips from that study, and together, see how well we do in discerning the babies' emotions.
transcript.translation: 事实上，我们将观看该研究中的一些视频片段，并一起看看我们在辨别婴儿情绪方面做得如何。

transcript.text: Today, I'd like to talk about the dangers of being too collaborative.
transcript.translation: 今天，我想谈谈过于合作的危险。

transcript.text: Being a good team player is an essential skill in our modern workplace.
transcript.translation: 在我们现代工作场所中，做一个好的团队合作者是一项必不可少的技能。

transcript.text: The ability to work well with others and collaborate on projects is a sought-after ability in nearly every position.
transcript.translation: 与他人良好合作并在项目上协作的能力在几乎每个职位中都备受青睐。

transcript.text: However, placing too much emphasis on being a good team player can negatively affect your career growth.
transcript.translation: 然而，过分强调做一个好的团队合作者可能会对你的职业发展产生负面影响。

transcript.text: Don't be overly focused on gaining consensus.
transcript.translation: 不要过度专注于达成共识。

transcript.text: Don't be too concerned with the opinions of others.
transcript.translation: 不要过于在意他人的意见。

transcript.text: This can hinder your ability to make decisions, speak up, and gain recognition for your individual skills and strengths.
transcript.translation: 这可能会阻碍你做决策、发言以及获得对个人技能和优势的认可。

transcript.text: Some people are too subordinate to others' opinions, too focused on decision consensus, too silent about their own points of view, too agreeable to take things on when they don't have time or energy.
transcript.translation: 有些人过于顺从他人的意见，过于专注于决策共识，对自己的观点过于沉默，在没有时间或精力时过于愿意承担任务。

transcript.text: This leads to building a brand of under-confident, submissive, low-impact non-leaders and hampers their growth and career advancement.
transcript.translation: 这会导致形成一种缺乏自信、顺从、低影响力的非领导者形象，并阻碍他们的成长和职业晋升。

transcript.text: Collaboration certainly makes your individual competencies and contributions more difficult for outsiders to identify.
transcript.translation: 合作确实使你的个人能力和贡献更难被外人识别。

transcript.text: Collaborative projects mean you're sharing the spotlight with others.
transcript.translation: 合作项目意味着你在与他人分享聚光灯。

transcript.text: Outsiders may then find it difficult to determine your contributions and strengths.
transcript.translation: 外人可能因此难以确定你的贡献和优势。

transcript.text: This may end up costing you opportunities for promotions or pay raises.
transcript.translation: 这最终可能会让你失去晋升或加薪的机会。

transcript.text: You certainly shouldn't ditch teamwork, but how can you avoid the hazards of being an over-collaborator?
transcript.translation: 你当然不应该抛弃团队合作，但如何避免成为一个过度合作者的风险呢？

transcript.text: Working in a team can have huge benefits.
transcript.translation: 在团队中工作可以带来巨大的好处。

transcript.text: Your team may have repeated successes and often gain recognition.
transcript.translation: 你的团队可能会反复取得成功并经常获得认可。

transcript.text: You'll then have more opportunities to expand your professional network than if you worked alone.
transcript.translation: 与独自工作相比，你将有更多机会扩展你的专业网络。

transcript.text: However, finding a balance between team efforts and individual projects that give you independent recognition is important for making a name for yourself and providing opportunities for advancement.
transcript.translation: 然而，在团队努力和个人项目之间找到平衡，这些项目能给你独立的认可，对于建立自己的名声和提供晋升机会很重要。

transcript.text: Be selective in who you work with.
transcript.translation: 在选择合作伙伴时要有选择性。

transcript.text: This will maximise the benefits and minimise the downsides of being a team player.
transcript.translation: 这将最大化作为一个团队合作者的好处，并最小化其弊端。

transcript.text: Collaborate with people who have complementary expertise.
transcript.translation: 与拥有互补专业知识的人合作。

transcript.text: Select projects where there's potential for mutual benefit.
transcript.translation: 选择有互惠互利潜力的项目。

transcript.text: Perhaps you're bringing your unique knowledge and gaining access to someone else's professional network.
transcript.translation: 或许你带来了你的独特知识，并获得了进入他人专业网络的机会。

transcript.text: Or maybe you're able to learn a new skill by working with someone.
transcript.translation: 或者也许你通过与某人合作能够学到一项新技能。

transcript.text: Seek out your teammates purposefully rather than jumping on every new group project opportunity.
transcript.translation: 有目的地寻找你的队友，而不是盲目抓住每一个新的团队项目机会。

transcript.text: When we are too collaborative, we want everyone to agree with a decision before we proceed.
transcript.translation: 当我们过于合作时，我们希望每个人在行动前都同意一个决定。

paragraphs.text: When considering risk factors associated with serious chronic diseases, we often think about health indicators such as cholesterol, blood pressure, and body weight. But poor diet and physical inactivity also each increase the risk of heart disease and have a role to play in the development of some cancers. Perhaps worse, the __26__ effects of an unhealthy diet and insufficient exercise are not limited to your body. Recent research has also shown that __27__ in a high-fat and high-sugar diet may have negative effects on your brain, causing learning and memory __28__.
paragraphs.translation: 在考虑与严重慢性病相关的风险因素时，我们通常会想到胆固醇、血压和体重等健康指标。但不良饮食和缺乏运动也会各自增加患心脏病的风险，并在某些癌症的发展中起到一定作用。更糟糕的是，不健康饮食和运动不足的后果不仅限于身体。最近的研究还表明，沉迷于高脂肪和高糖饮食可能对大脑产生负面影响，导致学习和记忆缺陷。

paragraphs.text: Studies have found obesity is associated with impairments in cognitive functioning, as __29__ by a range of learning and memory tests, such as the ability to remember a list of words presented some minutes or hours earlier. There is also a growing body of evidence that diet-induced cognitive impairments can emerge __30__ within weeks or even days. For example, one study found healthy adults __31__ to a high-fat diet for five days showed impaired attention, memory, and mood compared with a low-fat diet control group. Another study also found eating a high-fat and high-sugar breakfast each day for as little as four days resulted in problems with learning and memory __32__ to those observed in overweight and obese individuals.
paragraphs.translation: 研究发现，肥胖与认知功能受损相关，这通过一系列学习和记忆测试来评估，例如记住几分钟或几小时前呈现的单词列表的能力。还有越来越多的证据表明，饮食引起的认知障碍可能在几周甚至几天内迅速出现。例如，一项研究发现，被分配高脂肪饮食五天的健康成年人与低脂肪饮食对照组相比，注意力、记忆和情绪都出现了受损。另一项研究还发现，每天吃高脂肪和高糖早餐仅四天，就会导致学习和记忆问题，类似于在超重和肥胖个体中观察到的情况。

paragraphs.text: Body weight was not hugely different between the groups eating a healthy diet and those on high fat and sugar diets. So this shows negative __33__ of poor dietary intake can occur even when body weight has not changed __34__. Thus, body weight is not always the best indicator of health and a thin person still needs to eat well and exercise __35__.
paragraphs.translation: 在健康饮食组和高脂肪高糖饮食组之间，体重没有巨大差异。因此，这表明不良饮食摄入的负面影响可能在体重没有变化的情况下发生。因此，体重并不总是健康的最佳指标，瘦人仍然需要健康饮食和定期锻炼。

questionGroups.title: Increased Screen Time and Wellbeing Decline in Youth

material.title: Increased Screen Time and Wellbeing Decline in Youth

paragraphs.text: [A] Have young people never had it so good? Or do they face more challenges than any previous generation? Our current era in the West is one of high wealth. This means minors enjoy material benefits and legal protections that would have been the envy of those living in the past. But there is an increasing suspicion that all is not well for our youth. And one of the most popular explanations, among some experts and the popular media, is that excessive "screen time", is to blame. (This refers to all the attention young people devote to their phones, tablets and laptops.) However, this is a contentious theory and such claims have been treated skeptically by some scholars based on their reading of the relevant data.
paragraphs.translation: [A] 年轻人从未有过如此好的境遇吗？还是他们面临着比任何前代人都更多的挑战？我们西方当前的时代是一个高财富的时代。这意味着未成年人享有过去人们会羡慕的物质利益和法律保护。但越来越多的人怀疑年轻人的状况并不乐观。在一些专家和流行媒体中，最流行的解释之一是，过度的“屏幕时间”是罪魁祸首。（这指的是年轻人投入到手机、平板电脑和笔记本电脑上的所有注意力。）然而，这是一个有争议的理论，一些学者基于他们对相关数据的阅读，对此持怀疑态度。

paragraphs.text: [B] Now a new study has provided another contribution to the debate, uncovering strong evidence that adolescent wellbeing in the United States really is experiencing a decline and arguing that the most likely cause is the electronic riches we have given them. The background to this is that from the 1960s into the early 2000s, measures of average wellbeing went up in the US. This was especially true for younger people. It reflected the fact that these decades saw a climb in general standards of living and avoidance of mass societal traumas like full-scale war or economic deprivation. However, the "screen time" hypothesis, advanced by researchers such as Jean Twenge, is that electronic devices and excessive time spent online may have reversed these trends in recent years, causing problems for young people's psychological health.
paragraphs.translation: [B] 现在，一项新研究为这场辩论提供了另一份贡献，揭示了强有力的证据，表明美国青少年的幸福感确实在下降，并认为最可能的原因是我们给予他们的电子财富。其背景是，从20世纪60年代到21世纪初，美国的平均幸福感指标有所上升。这对年轻人尤其如此。这反映了这些年代生活水平普遍提高，并避免了像全面战争或经济匮乏这样的大规模社会创伤。然而，由研究者如琼·特温奇提出的“屏幕时间”假设认为，电子设备和过度上网时间可能在近年来逆转了这些趋势，导致年轻人的心理健康问题。

paragraphs.text: [C] To investigate, Twenge and her colleagues dived into the "Monitoring the Future" dataset based on annual surveys of American school students from grades 8, 10, and 12 that started in 1991. In total, 1.1 million young people answered various questions related to their wellbeing. Twenge's team's analysis of the answers confirmed the earlier, well-established wellbeing climb, with scores rising across the 1990s, and into the later 2000s. This was found across measures like self-esteem, life satisfaction, happiness and satisfaction with individual domains like job, neighborhood, or friends. But around 2012 these measures started to decline. This continued through 2016, the most recent year for which data is available.
paragraphs.translation: [C] 为了进行调查，特温奇和她的同事们深入研究了基于始于1991年的美国8年级、10年级和12年级学生年度调查的“监测未来”数据集。总共有110万年轻人回答了与他们幸福感相关的各种问题。特温奇团队对答案的分析证实了早期建立的幸福感上升趋势，分数在20世纪90年代和21世纪初有所上升。这在自尊、生活满意度、幸福感以及对工作、邻居或朋友等个人领域的满意度等指标中都有发现。但大约在2012年，这些指标开始下降。这种情况一直持续到2016年，这是有数据可查的最近一年。

paragraphs.text: [D] Twenge and her colleagues wanted to understand why this change in average wellbeing occurred. However, it is very hard to demonstrate causes using non-experimental data such as this. In fact, when Twenge previously used this data to suggest a screen time effect, some commentators were quick to raise this problem. They argued that her causal-sounding claims rested on correlational data, and that she had not adequately accounted for other potential causal factors. This time around, Twenge and her team make a point of saying that they are not trying to establish causes as such, but that they are assessing the plausibility of potential causes.
paragraphs.translation: [D] 特温奇和她的同事们想理解为什么平均幸福感发生了这种变化。然而，使用像这样的非实验数据来证明因果关系是非常困难的。事实上，当特温奇之前使用这些数据来暗示屏幕时间效应时，一些评论者很快提出了这个问题。他们认为她听起来像因果关系的陈述依赖于相关数据，而且她没有充分考虑其他潜在的因果因素。这次，特温奇和她的团队特别指出，他们不是试图建立因果关系，而是在评估潜在原因的可行性。

paragraphs.text: [E] First, they explain that if a given variable is playing a role in affecting wellbeing, then we should expect any change in that variable to correlate with the observed changes in wellbeing. If not, it is not plausible that the variable is a causal factor. So the researchers looked at time spent in a number of activities that could plausibly be driving the wellbeing decline. Less sport, and fewer meetings with peers correlated with lower wellbeing, as did less time reading print media(newspapers) and, surprisingly, less time doing homework .(This last finding would appear to contradict another popular hypothesis that it is our burdening of students with assignments that is causing all the problems.) In addition, more TV watching and more electronic communication both correlated with lower wellbeing. All these effects held true for measures of happiness, life satisfaction and self-esteem, with the effects stronger in the 8th and 10th-graders.
paragraphs.translation: [E] 首先，他们解释说，如果某个变量在影响幸福感方面发挥作用，那么我们应该期望该变量的任何变化都与观察到的幸福感变化相关。如果不是，那么该变量是因果因素就不合理。因此，研究人员查看了在可能导致幸福感下降的一些活动上花费的时间。运动减少，与同龄人见面减少，与幸福感较低相关，阅读印刷媒体（报纸）的时间减少，以及令人惊讶的是，做作业的时间减少也是如此。（后一个发现似乎与另一个流行假设矛盾，即用作业负担学生是导致所有问题的原因。）此外，看电视更多和电子通信更多都与幸福感较低相关。所有这些影响在幸福感、生活满意度和自尊的测量中都成立，且在8年级和10年级学生中影响更强。

paragraphs.text: [F] Next, Twenge's team dug a little deeper into the data on screen time. They found that adolescents who spent a very small amount of time on digital devices—a couple of hours a week—had the highest wellbeing. Their wellbeing was even higher than those who never used such devices. However, higher doses of screen time were clearly associated with lower happiness. Those spending 10-19 hours per week on their devices were 41 percent more likely to be unhappy than lower-frequency users. Those who used such devices 40 hours a week or more(one in ten teenagers) were twice as likely to be unhappy. The data was slightly complicated by the fact that there was a tendency for kids who were social in the real world to also use more online communication, but by bracketing out different cases it became clear that the real-world sociality component correlated with greater wellbeing, whereas greater time on screens or online only correlated with poorer wellbeing.
paragraphs.translation: [F] 接下来，特温奇的团队更深入地研究了屏幕时间数据。他们发现，在数字设备上花费很少时间（每周几小时）的青少年幸福感最高。他们的幸福感甚至高于那些从不使用这些设备的人。然而，更高的屏幕时间剂量显然与较低的幸福相关。每周在设备上花费10-19小时的人比低频使用者不快乐的可能性高41%。每周使用这些设备40小时或更多（十分之一的青少年）的人不快乐的可能性是两倍。数据有点复杂，因为事实上，在现实世界中社交的孩子也倾向于使用更多在线通信，但通过排除不同情况，很明显现实世界的社交部分与更大的幸福感相关，而在屏幕上或网上花费更多时间只与较差的幸福感相关。

paragraphs.text: [G] So far, so plausible. But the next question is, are the drops in average wellbeing happening at the same time as trends toward increased electronic device usage? It looks like it-after all, 2012 was the tipping point when more than half of Americans began owning smartphones. Twenge and her colleagues also found that across the key years of 2013-16, wellbeing was indeed lowest in years where adolescents spent more time online, on social media, and reading news online, and when more youth in the United States had smartphones. And in a second analysis, they found that where technology went, dips in wellbeing followed. For instance, years with a larger increase in online usage were followed by years with lower wellbeing, rather than the other way around. This does not prove causality, but is consistent with it. Meanwhile, TV use did not show this tracking. TV might make you less happy, but this is not what seems to be driving the recent declines in young people's average happiness.
paragraphs.translation: [G] 到目前为止，这似乎合理。但下一个问题是，平均幸福感的下降是否与电子设备使用增加的趋势同时发生？看起来是这样——毕竟，2012年是超过一半美国人开始拥有智能手机的转折点。特温奇和她的同事还发现，在2013-16的关键年份里，幸福感确实在青少年更多时间上网、使用社交媒体和在线阅读新闻，以及更多美国青少年拥有智能手机的年份最低。在第二次分析中，他们发现技术发展到哪里，幸福感的下降就随之而来。例如，在线使用量增加较大的年份之后是幸福感较低的年份，而不是相反。这并不能证明因果关系，但与因果关系一致。同时，电视使用没有显示出这种跟踪。电视可能会让你不那么快乐，但这似乎不是导致年轻人平均幸福感最近下降的原因。

paragraphs.text: [H] A similar but reversed pattern was found for the activities associated with greater wellbeing. For example, years when people spent more time with friends were better years for wellbeing (and followed by better years). Sadly, the data also showed face-to-face socializing and sports activity had declined over the period covered by the survey.
paragraphs.translation: [H] 对于与更大幸福感相关的活动，发现了一种相似但相反的模式。例如，当人们花更多时间与朋友相处的年份，幸福感更好（并且随后年份也更好）。遗憾的是，数据还显示，在调查涵盖的期间，面对面的社交和体育活动有所下降。

paragraphs.text: [I] There is another explanation that Twenge and her colleagues wanted to address: the impact of the great recession of 2007-2009, which hit a great number of American families and might be affecting adolescents. The dataset they used did not include economic data, so instead the researchers looked at whether the 2013-16 wellbeing decline was tracking economic indicators. They found some evidence that some crude measures, like income inequality, correlated with changes in wellbeing, but economic measures with a more direct impact, like family income and unemployment rates (which put families into difficulties), had no relationship with wellbeing. The researchers also note that the recession hit some years before we see the beginning of the wellbeing drop, and before the steepest wellbeing decline, which occurred in 2013.
paragraphs.translation: [I] 还有另一种解释是特温和她的同事们想解决的：2007-2009年大衰退的影响，它打击了许多美国家庭，并可能影响青少年。他们使用的数据集不包括经济数据，因此研究人员转而查看2013-16年的幸福感下降是否跟踪经济指标。他们发现一些证据表明，一些粗略的衡量指标，如收入不平等，与幸福感的变化相关，但具有更直接影响的经济衡量指标，如家庭收入和失业率（这使家庭陷入困境），与幸福感没有关系。研究人员还指出，衰退发生在我们看到幸福感下降开始的几年前，并且在2013年最陡峭的幸福感下降之前。

paragraphs.text: [J] The researchers conclude that electronic communication was the only adolescent activity that increased at the same time psychological wellbeing declined. I suspect that some experts in the field will be keen to address alternative explanations, such as unassessed variables playing a role in the wellbeing decline. But the new work does go further than previous research and suggests that screen time should still be considered a potential barrier to young people's flourishing.
paragraphs.translation: [J] 研究人员得出结论，电子通信是唯一在心理健康下降的同时增加的青少年活动。我怀疑该领域的一些专家会热衷于解决其他解释，如未评估的变量在幸福感下降中起作用。但这项新工作确实比以前的研究更进一步，并建议屏幕时间仍应被视为年轻人繁荣的潜在障碍。

questionGroups.title: Passage One

paragraphs.text: "The dangerous thing about lying is people don't understand how the act changes us." says Dan Ariely, behavioural psychologist at Duke University. Psychologists have documented children lying as early as the age of two. Some experts even consider lying a developmental milestone, like crawling and walking, because it requires sophisticated planning, attention and the ability to see a situation from someone else's perspective to manipulate them. But, for most people, lying gets limited as we develop a sense of morality and the ability to self-regulate.
paragraphs.translation: "谎言的危险之处在于，人们不了解这种行为如何改变我们。"杜克大学行为心理学家丹·阿里利说。心理学家记录到儿童早在两岁时就会说谎。一些专家甚至认为说谎是一个发展里程碑，就像爬行和走路一样，因为它需要复杂的计划、注意力以及从他人视角看待情境以操纵他们的能力。但是，对大多数人来说，随着我们发展出道德感和自我调节能力，说谎行为会受到限制。

paragraphs.text: Harvard cognitive neuroscientist Joshua Greene says, for most of us, lying takes work. In studies, he gave subjects a chance to deceive for monetary gain while examining their brains in a functional MRI machine, which maps blood flow to active parts of the brain. Some people told the truth instantly and instinctively. But others opted to lie, and they showed increased activity in their frontal parietal (颅腔壁的) control network, which is involved in difficult or complex thinking. This suggests that they were deciding between truth and dishonesty and ultimately opting for the letter. For a follow-up analysis, he found that people whose neural (神经的) reward centers were more active when they won money were also more likely to be among the group of liars suggesting that lying may have to do with the inability to resist temptation.
paragraphs.translation: 哈佛大学认知神经科学家约书亚·格林说，对我们大多数人来说，说谎需要付出努力。在研究中，他给受试者一个为金钱收益而欺骗的机会，同时使用功能性磁共振成像机检查他们的大脑，该机器能绘制大脑活跃部位的血流图。有些人立即本能地说了实话。但另一些人选择说谎，他们显示前顶叶（颅腔壁的）控制网络的活动增加，这与困难或复杂的思维有关。这表明他们在诚实与不诚实之间做决定，最终选择了后者。在后续分析中，他发现那些在赢钱时神经奖励中心更活跃的人，也更可能属于说谎者群体，这表明说谎可能与无法抵抗诱惑有关。

paragraphs.text: External conditions also matter in terms of when and how often we lie. We are more likely to lie, when we are able to rationalise it, when we are stressed and fatigued or see others being dishonest. And we are less likely to lie when we have moral reminders or when we think others are watching. "We as a society need to understand that, when we don't punish lying, we increase the probability it will happen again." Ariely says.
paragraphs.translation: 外部条件在说谎的时间和频率方面也很重要。当我们能够合理化说谎时，当我们感到压力和疲劳或看到他人不诚实时，我们更可能说谎。而当我们有道德提醒或认为别人在看着时，我们更不可能说谎。"作为一个社会，我们需要明白，当我们不惩罚说谎时，我们增加了它再次发生的概率。"阿里利说。

paragraphs.text: In a 2016 study published in the journal Nature Neuroscience, Ariely and colleagues showed how dishonesty alters people's brains, making it easier to tell ties in the future. When people uttered a falsehood, the scientists noticed a burst of activity in their amygdala. The amygdala is a crucial part of the brain that produces fear, anxiety and emotional responses— including that sinking, guilty feeling you get when you lie. But when scientists had their subjects play a game in which they won money by deceiving their partner, they noticed the negative signals from the amygdala began to decrease. Not only that, but when people faced no consequences for dishonesty, their falsehood tended to get even more sensational. This means that if you give people multiple opportunities to lie for their own benefit, they start with little lies which get bigger over time.
paragraphs.translation: 在2016年发表于《自然·神经科学》期刊的一项研究中，阿里利及其同事展示了不诚实如何改变人们的大脑，使未来更容易说谎。当人们说出谎言时，科学家注意到他们杏仁核的活动爆发。杏仁核是大脑的一个关键部分，产生恐惧、焦虑和情绪反应——包括说谎时那种下沉的、内疚的感觉。但当科学家让受试者玩一个通过欺骗伙伴赢钱的游戏时，他们注意到杏仁核的负面信号开始减少。不仅如此，当人们为不诚实行为不面临任何后果时，他们的谎言往往变得更加耸人听闻。这意味着，如果你给人们多次为自身利益说谎的机会，他们会从小谎言开始，随着时间的推移，谎言会越来越大。

questionGroups.title: Passage Two

paragraphs.text: Here's how the Pacific Northwest is preparing for "The Big One". It's the mother of all disaster drills for what could be the worst disaster in American history. California has spent years preparing for "The Big One"—the inevitable earthquake that will undoubtedly unleash all kinds of havoc along the famous San Andreas fault (断层). But what if the fault that runs along the Pacific Northwest delivers a gigantic earthquake of its own? If the people of the Cascadia region have anything to do with it, they won't be caught unawares.
paragraphs.translation: 以下是太平洋西北地区如何为'大地震'做准备。这可能是美国历史上最严重灾难的顶级演习。加利福尼亚州多年来一直在为'大地震'做准备——这场不可避免的地震无疑将在著名的圣安德烈亚斯断层上造成各种破坏。但如果沿着太平洋西北地区的断层也发生一场巨大地震呢？如果卡斯卡迪亚地区的民众有所准备，他们就不会措手不及。

paragraphs.text: The region is engaged in a multi-day earthquake-and-tsunami (海啸) drill involving around 20,000 people. The Cascadia Rising drill gives area residents and emergency responders a chance to practice what to do in case of a 9.0-magnitude earthquake and tsunami along one of the nation's dangerous—and underestimated—faults.
paragraphs.translation: 该地区正在进行一场涉及约2万人的多日地震和海啸演习。卡斯卡迪亚上升演习让当地居民和应急响应人员有机会练习在沿该国一条危险且被低估的断层发生9.0级地震和海啸时该怎么做。

paragraphs.text: The Cascadia Earthquake Zone is big enough to compete with San Andreas (it's been called the most dangerous fault in America), but it's much lesser known than its California cousin. Nearly 700 miles long, the earthquake zone is located by the North American Plate off the coast of Pacific British Columbia, Washington, Oregon and Northern California.
paragraphs.translation: 卡斯卡迪亚地震带足够大，可以与圣安德烈亚斯断层竞争（它被称为美国最危险的断层），但它比其加利福尼亚的对应部分远不为人所知。这条地震带长近700英里，位于北美板块沿不列颠哥伦比亚省、华盛顿州、俄勒冈州和北加利福尼亚州海岸的位置。

paragraphs.text: Cascadia is what's known as a "megathrust" fault. Megathrusts are created in earthquake zones—land plate boundaries where two plates converge. In the areas where one plate is beneath another, stress builds up over time. During a megathrust event, all of that stress releases and some of the world's most powerful earthquakes occur. Remember the 9.1 earthquake and tsunami in the Indian Ocean off Sumatra in 2004? It was caused by a megathrust event as the India plate moved beneath the Burma micro-plate.
paragraphs.translation: 卡斯卡迪亚是一种被称为'大型逆冲断层'的断层。逆冲断层形成于地震带——即两个板块汇聚的陆地板块边界。在一个板块位于另一个板块之下的区域，应力随时间积累。在一次逆冲事件中，所有这些应力释放，导致一些世界上最强烈的地震发生。还记得2004年印度洋苏门答腊岛附近发生的9.1级地震和海啸吗？它是由印度板块移动到缅甸微板块之下的逆冲事件引起的。

paragraphs.text: The last time a major earthquake occurred along the Cascadia fault was in 1700, so officials worry that another event could occur any time. To prevent that event from becoming a catastrophe, first responders will join members of the public in rehearsals that involve communication, evacuation, search and rescue, and other scenarios.
paragraphs.translation: 上一次沿卡斯卡迪亚断层发生大地震是在1700年，因此官员们担心另一次事件可能随时发生。为了防止该事件演变成灾难，急救人员将与公众一起参与涉及通讯、疏散、搜救和其他场景的演习。

paragraphs.text: Thousands of casualties are expected if a 9.0 earthquake were to occur. First, the earthquake would shake metropolitan areas including Seattle and Portland. This could trigger a tsunami that would create havoc along the coast. Not all casualties can necessarily be prevented—but by coordinating across local, state, and even national borders, officials hope that the worst-case scenario can be averted. On the exercise's website, officials explain that the report they prepare during this rehearsal will inform disaster management for years to come.
paragraphs.translation: 如果发生9.0级地震，预计会有数千人伤亡。首先，地震将震动包括西雅图和波特兰在内的大都市区。这可能引发海啸，在沿海地区造成破坏。并非所有伤亡都能被阻止——但通过跨越地方、州甚至国家边界的协调，官员们希望最坏情况情景能够避免。在演习网站上，官员们解释说，他们在这次演习中准备的报告将为未来多年的灾害管理提供信息。

paragraphs.text: For hundreds of thousands of Cascadia residents. "The Big One" isn't a question of if, only when. And it's never too early to get ready for the inevitable.
paragraphs.translation: 对于数十万卡斯卡迪亚居民来说，'大地震'不是是否会发生的问题，而是什么时候发生的问题。而且，为不可避免的事情做准备永远不会太早。

questionGroups.sourceText: 荷花(lotus flower)是中国的名花之一，深受人们喜爱。中国许多地方的湖泊和池塘都适宜荷花生长。荷花色彩鲜艳，夏日清晨绽放，夜晚闭合。花期长达两三个月，吸引来自各地的游客前往观赏。荷花具有多种功能，既能绿化水面，又能美化庭园，还可净化水质、减少污染、改善环境。荷花迎骄阳而不惧，出污泥而不染，象征纯洁、高雅，常常用来比喻人的高尚品德，历来是诗人画家创作的重要题材。荷花盛开的地方也是许多摄影爱好者经常光顾之地。

answer.modelTranslation: The lotus flower is one of China's famous flowers, deeply loved by people. Many lakes and ponds in China are suitable for the growth of lotus flowers. With their vibrant colors, lotus flowers bloom in the early morning of summer and close at night. Their blooming period lasts for two to three months, attracting tourists from all over to admire them. Lotus flowers have multiple functions; they can green the water surface, beautify gardens, purify water quality, reduce pollution, and improve the environment. Facing the scorching sun without fear and emerging from the mud unsoiled, lotus flowers symbolize purity and elegance, often used to metaphorically describe noble character, and have always been an important subject for poets and painters. Places where lotus flowers are in full bloom are also frequently visited by many photography enthusiasts.
